clue.text: A main course?

blocks.note: surface reading: the central dish of a dinner
setter's reading: 'the main' is an old name for the open sea, so this is a route followed across it

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: 'main' means the ocean, and a 'course' is a route vessels take.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy recognised sea route used regularly by merchant vessels is exactly a course across the ocean.

clue.text: Paid tribute to an old music-maker in blue

indicators.note: in places the instrument inside the word for blue, which surrounds it

blocks.note: a stringed instrument of earlier centuries

explanation.surface: Someone honours a vintage instrument while feeling melancholy.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to honour or acknowledge them publicly, a formal mark of respect.

clue.text: Risk changing nothing, me being tiresome!

indicators.note: something changing takes a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A grumble that refusing to take any chances is making the speaker dull company.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome describes something annoying or wearisome, a close synonym for tedious and trying.

clue.text: Enter enclosure with speed, holding film

indicators.note: the outer words hold the film inside them, as hands hold an object

blocks.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
E.T., Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: Someone races into a compound while carrying a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' acts on the joined pair 'enclosure with speed', so the film sits at the join between them rather than inside either one.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate is to pass into or get inside something, so it replaces the verb meaning go in.

clue.text: Brings in a backstreet number

indicators.note: back tells us to read the following pieces from the end to the start

blocks.note: the street part of this word is abbreviated in the usual way; its first half is the signal

explanation.surface: Someone earns money from a house number in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' splits into 'back' and 'street'. NETTS is a variant spelling of nets, as in earning a net profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To nett a sum is to earn it as clear profit after costs, meaning to gain or take home income.

clue.text: After chopping up a log, bum gets backache

indicators.note: chopping up breaks things into pieces that can be put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A tramp splits firewood and pays for it with a sore back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the muscles and joints of the lower spine, a medical name for lower back pain.

clue.text: Telephone college back with a short message

indicators.note: back says the phone and college pieces are read from right to left

blocks.note: TEL is the standard abbreviation for telephone
Eton, the famous English public school

explanation.surface: An instruction to ring a college office back and leave a brief note.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is a famous private boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet of notepaper used for writing brief letters or messages.

clue.text: They ensure you can hear vulgar people talking

blocks.note: loud can mean brash or tasteless

explanation.surface: A quip that coarse people talking are always audible.
explanation.definitionFit: Loudspeakers are devices that amplify sound, so their whole job is making audio audible to listeners.

clue.text: Waterproof cloth produced in kilos

indicators.note: produced suggests something made up out of raw material, here re-made from letters

explanation.surface: Rainproof fabric being made and sold by the kilogram.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskin is cotton treated with oil so rain runs off it, a classic weatherproof fabric for coats.

clue.text: Relief worker, Edward, is put to the test

blocks.note: a temp fills in for a regular employee
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A stand-in worker called Edward faces a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief worker' suggests aid work, but a relief here is a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempted has an older biblical sense of tried or tested, as when Christ was tempted in the wilderness.

clue.text: Gives data and sorted out trouble

indicators.note: sorted out implies items put into a fresh order, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone supplies information and resolves a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out trouble' reads like fixing a problem, but 'trouble' is the definition and 'sorted out' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage is an unfavourable condition or drawback, which is a problem or difficulty for someone.

clue.text: US city editor touring West End

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the letters wander into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An American journalist visiting London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district but means the last letter of West. The West End is central London's entertainment area.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the largest city in Michigan, famous for car manufacturing and Motown.

clue.text: They contain stalls fixed to pole

explanation.surface: Market stalls or booths attached to a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalls' suggests market traders or theatre seats; here they are compartments for horses. 'Pole' is one of the Earth's poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Stables are buildings for horses, divided internally into separate compartments for each animal.

clue.text: Chaplain wants cushion he dropped here

indicators.note: dropped means let fall or left out, so a part is taken away

blocks.note: a pad is a soft cushion

explanation.surface: A clergyman asks for a cushion that a man let fall in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE from HERE to leave RE. Padre is a forces term for a chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal title for a military chaplain, from the Spanish and Italian for father.

clue.text: Insulted on interrupting a fellow with Father Ted

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so this word goes inside the others

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence at being interrupted while watching the sitcom Father Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a 1990s TV sitcom about Irish priests; the title reads as one name but splits into two pieces here.
explanation.definitionFit: To be affronted is to be offended by a slight or open disrespect, which matches feeling insulted.

clue.text: Bank chap whose accounts are often exaggerated?

definitions.text: Bank chap whose accounts are often exaggerated?

blocks.clueFragment: Bank chap whose accounts are often exaggerated?
blocks.note: surface reading: a bank employee who inflates the figures in customers' accounts

blocks.clueFragment: Bank chap whose accounts are often exaggerated?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a man sitting on a river bank whose stories of the one that got away grow in the telling

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' and 'accounts' both suggest finance, but the bank is a riverside and the accounts are tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers are proverbial for boasting about the size of their catch, and they sit on riverbanks.

clue.text: Sailor despatched to look round for missing people

indicators.note: turning round faces the other way, so the word for look is read backwards

explanation.surface: A sailor is sent out to search for people who have gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Absentees are those who are not present where expected, such as at work or school.

clue.text: Somewhere from southern Spain and Portugal

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the Iberian peninsula holds both countries

explanation.surface: A place lying in the south of the Iberian peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to southern Iberia, but the answer is a vast region of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is a vast region of northern Asia, so it is simply a place, deliberately vague as a definition.

clue.text: Are going into home the shortest distance away

indicators.note: going into a place means entering it, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Settling into the house that lies closest by.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest is the superlative of near, describing whatever lies closest in space.

clue.text: Reptile old boy found in new car

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so these letters are rearranged
found in means located inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: OB, old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A snake and a former pupil are discovered inside a newly bought car.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobra is a venomous snake, and snakes are reptiles, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: Typical of girl one found in cricket club

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the girl and one are placed within

blocks.note: CC is the abbreviation for cricket club
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: It is normal for a young woman to turn up at the cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic can mean a perfect representative example of its kind, a model or textbook instance.

clue.text: Gold ring found in rubbish at home

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the ring is placed within the home piece

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A gold ring turns up amid the household junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold ring' reads as one item, but the definition and the wordplay part company between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullion is gold or silver in bulk, as bars or ingots, valued by weight.

clue.text: Include half of them needing support

indicators.note: half of a word means keeping just one of its two halves

explanation.surface: Half of some group requires help to be counted in.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace can mean to contain or take in as part of a whole, as a range embraces many styles.

clue.text: Moral principle described in one thick volume

indicators.note: described in suggests sitting within the text, so the answer is inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding completing the picture of a book

explanation.surface: An ethical rule set out in a single fat book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' just completes the surface picture of a weighty book.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a code or standard of right conduct, a guiding belief about how to behave.

clue.text: It may be shouldered by a man in uniform

definitions.text: It may be shouldered by a man in uniform

blocks.clueFragment: It may be shouldered by a man in uniform
blocks.note: surface reading: something a soldier carries on his shoulder, like a rifle

blocks.clueFragment: It may be shouldered by a man in uniform
blocks.note: setter's reading: an ornamental piece worn on the shoulder of a uniform

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shouldered' suggests carrying a weapon or burden, but it literally sits on the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulet is a decorative shoulder strap or fringe on military and naval uniforms.

clue.text: Scream to see church taking credit

indicators.note: taking in something means holding it inside, so credit sits within

blocks.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A shriek on discovering a church buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh, high-pitched cry, which is what a scream sounds like.

clue.text: Gathering for a church service in Gateshead

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Mass is the Catholic Eucharist service
the first letter of the Gate part of this town name

explanation.surface: A meeting arranged for a service at a church in Gateshead.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England, but here it splits into 'Gate' and 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Massing means assembling into a large group, which is a gathering together of people or things.

clue.text: Innocent chap becomes a furniture remover

indicators.note: becomes signals turning into something different, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blameless man takes a job carrying furniture for house moves.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantechnicon is an old British word for a large removal van.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantechnicon is a big lorry used to move household goods, so it carries furniture away.
